# Template: bar_race
A bar chart race: one horizontal bar per racer, the rows REORDERING as the numbers change, drawn as ink so it animates as geometry. `values` is a list of lists — STAGES of the same field, one row per stage and one number per racer — and the numeric `stage` param picks which one is shown. A fractional stage interpolates the bar lengths AND the rank, so `animate: {stage: 59}` with `easing: "linear"` plays the whole race at one steady speed. `top_n` bounds the field (default 10) and a racer climbing into it slides in and fades up instead of popping; `order: "fixed"` keeps the input order and animates lengths only. Write `null` (never 0) for a racer not in the field at a stage — it is ranked last, drawn as nothing, and arrives at its real value rather than growing into it. Two racers swapping places share one row for the instant of the overtake, so their names and values coincide there: that is BY DESIGN — it is what an overtake looks like, and snapping the ranks instead is the defect this scene exists to avoid. Both labels dim as they meet and brighten again as they part, so the crossing reads as ink laid over ink. The scale follows the leader, so the early stages are never squashed flat, and its ticks slide rather than reflow; `xlim` fixes the range instead. `ticker` writes the year large and dim in the plot's corner, and every bar carries its own value unless `value_labels: false`. Horizontal by default, because that is where long racer names fit; `orientation: "vertical"` stands the bars up as columns with the names underneath and caps the field at 12. Feed it typed numbers, or a code element's variables via "{id.var}" tokens (type the labels by hand so the race_i beats exist before the script has run). Choose this scene for ANY request for a bar chart race, a leaderboard over time, "who overtook whom", or ranks changing year by year. Up to 200 stages and 40 racers, but a script's harvest caps at 5000 numbers — 20 racers × 200 stages fits, 40 racers × 200 stages does not.

Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the value axis with its caption and ticks
- note: the refusal note, drawn when no bar can have any length — every number in the race is zero or less, or every cell is an explicit null (every racer absent)
- race_1: the first racer's bar (its fill, name and value label; race_2, race_3, … likewise) — one per label, in INPUT order, at every stage
- ticker: the large stage caption (the year), when set
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Bar chart race of the four biggest economies from 1990 to 2020." → params: {"labels":["United States","China","Japan","Germany"],"values":[[6,0.4,3.1,1.8],[10.3,1.2,4.9,1.9],[15,6.1,5.7,3.4],[21.1,14.7,5,3.9]],"stage":0,"x_label":"GDP (trillion USD)","title":"The four biggest economies, 1990 → 2020"}
